Prevention: Destroy alternate weed hosts growing on field bunds, water channels and wastelands in the area.
Summer ploughing to expose the life stages of the pest.
Remove or avoid growing alternate host plants (e.g. congress weed, datura, milkweed, Chenopodium spp., okra, tomato and brinjal) in and around fields.
Do not throw uprooted weeds in water channel.
Use the crop rotation practices (e.g. rice or corn based on the availability of water and awareness of husbandry practices) and burn the plant debris to clean field
It is important to remember that mealybug crawlers spread through human interventions such as spraying, irrigations, frequent movement through the infected area etc., so avoid these activities.
Monitoring: Presence of ant colonies on the plants.
The mealybug body is covered with very short waxy filaments
It spreads from the borders of the field.
In initial stages, it can be observed in small pockets.
Take action when 5% of the plants are infested.
Direct Control: Encourage the activity of predators like
Cryptolaemus montrouzieri , Cheilomenes sexmaculata , also known as ladybird beetles.
A main vector of mealybug transmission is ants.
Therefore, controlling ants will allow predators to feed on mealybugs, reducing their numbers.
Restrictions: Mealybugs at initial stage appear in small pockets, therefore
recommended insecticides are applied only in the infested spot, not in the entire crop.
Locate ant colonies and destroy them with drenching of chlorpyriphos 20
This operation can be carried out round the year
Recommended doses of insecticides of carbamate (thiodicarb 75
EC @ 5l/ha) & add commercial stickers, spreaders or the khadhi soap (20gm / 10 lit of water) to degrade the waxy coating and spray rotation-wise in consecutive sprays.
